\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{प्रभातम्} (prabhātam)}{प्रभातम् (prabhātam)}]{\sk{प्रभातम्} (prabhātam) — morning, daybreak}

\label{lesson:SA-C91-prabhatam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for midnight, then the Sanskrit for dawn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{प्रभातम्}}
\textbf{\sk{प्रभातम्}} — \emph{prabhātam} — \textquotedblleft{}morning, daybreak\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Prabhāta} is the past participle of \emph{pra} + the root √bhā, \textquotedblleft{}to shine\textquotedblright{}: \textquotedblleft{}shone forth\textquotedblright{}, and so daybreak (MW, CDIAL 8707).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prabhātam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prabhātam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{prabhātam}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for midnight, then the Sanskrit for dawn, then say \emph{prabhātam} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{सन्ध्या} (sandhyā)}{सन्ध्या (sandhyā)}]{\sk{सन्ध्या} (sandhyā) — twilight}

\label{lesson:SA-C91-sandhya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for dawn, then the Sanskrit for morning.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{सन्ध्या}}
\textbf{\sk{सन्ध्या}} — \emph{sandhyā} — \textquotedblleft{}twilight\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
CDIAL 12918 explains \emph{sandhyā} as first a form of \emph{saṃdhi}, \textquotedblleft{}junction\textquotedblright{}: the joining of day and night. It lives on as Hindi \emph{sāṃjh}, \textquotedblleft{}evening\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sandhyā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{sandhyā}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for dawn, then the Sanskrit for morning, then say \emph{sandhyā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{हेमन्तः} (hemantaḥ)}{हेमन्तः (hemantaḥ)}]{\sk{हेमन्तः} (hemantaḥ) — early winter}

\label{lesson:SA-C91-hemantah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for morning, then the Sanskrit for twilight.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{हेमन्तः}}
\textbf{\sk{हेमन्तः}} — \emph{hemantaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}early winter\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Hemanta} is a Rigvedic word built on \emph{heman}, \textquotedblleft{}in winter\textquotedblright{}, which MW files beside \emph{hima}, \textquotedblleft{}cold, snow\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 14164).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{शिशिरः} (śiśiraḥ)}{शिशिरः (śiśiraḥ)}]{\sk{शिशिरः} (śiśiraḥ) — late winter}

\label{lesson:SA-C91-sisirah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for twilight, then the Sanskrit for early winter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{शिशिरः}}
\textbf{\sk{शिशिरः}} — \emph{śiśiraḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}late winter\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Śiśira} is probably connected with the root √śyai and with \emph{śīta}, \textquotedblleft{}cold\textquotedblright{} (MW, CDIAL 12475). It lives on as Hindi \emph{sisir}, \textquotedblleft{}cold, dew\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\textbf{\sk{शरद्}} — \emph{śarad} — \textquotedblleft{}autumn\textquotedblright{}.

\end{cousinweb}
